## Functional summary

This 490-amino-acid protein is **strongly predicted to be UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate–2,6-diaminopimelate ligase (MurE; EC 6.3.2.13)**, an ATP-dependent enzyme in bacterial peptidoglycan cell-wall biosynthesis.

It likely catalyzes the addition of meso-2,6-diaminopimelate to UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-Glu, producing the corresponding tripeptide precursor, ADP, and phosphate. The closest reviewed Swiss-Prot homolog reported by the tool is 53.8% identical across 98.4% of the query, supporting this functional assignment. The homolog annotation also indicates Mg²⁺ dependence and cytoplasmic localization; these are transferred by homology, not directly established for this sequence.

**Sequence-derived properties:** estimated molecular mass 51.96 kDa; theoretical pI 6.18; predicted charge at pH 7 of −5.24. These are computational estimates and do not account for processing or modifications.

**Evidence caveat:** The assignment is supported by close, near-full-length homologs, but the sequence itself has not been experimentally tested here. The tool did not establish the protein’s organism, oligomeric state, or activity experimentally.
